df.show()

# change it to rdd so that we can save the output as text file
df = df.rdd.saveAsTextFile('/home/hduser/Desktop/sample1/avg/')

# stop spark context

answer:
I believe the problem it could be the delimiter, I would recommend that you check on that. In the results you are getting only one column, instead the 4 that you are expecting.

You can read the from Spark like:

df = spark.read.option('delimiter', ',').csv(path_to_file)

Its save as DataFrame, if you are saving through Glue then I recommend that you create the DynamicDataFrame.

You can check the examples in this url:

https://sparkbyexamples.com/spark/write-read-csv-file-from-s3-into-dataframe/
